headline: European nations secure seat at upcoming Abu Dhabi peace talks on Ukraine
standfirst: France confirms European delegates will join upcoming U.S.-mediated negotiations in Abu Dhabi, despite initial resistance from Moscow.
keyPoints: France confirmed European representation at upcoming U.S.-mediated peace talks in Abu Dhabi.
The upcoming meetings are scheduled for Tuesday and Wednesday between officials from Ukraine, Russia, and the United States.
Russia previously indicated that European representatives should not have a place at the negotiating table.
U.S. envoy Jared Kushner stated that Washington plans to consult closely with European partners on the sidelines.

paragraphs: European officials are set to take part in upcoming United States-mediated negotiations in Abu Dhabi aimed at addressing the ongoing conflict in Ukraine. French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot confirmed the development on Sunday, noting that the country would be directly involved in the discussions. The upcoming sessions represent the first three-way round of negotiations of this specific format since the month of February.

The scheduled meetings, which are set for Tuesday and Wednesday, were originally framed strictly as a trilateral format involving officials from Ukraine, Russia, and the United States rather than heads of state. Specific identities regarding the individuals participating in the diplomatic sessions have not yet been made public by the organizing nations. While Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has consistently advocated for the inclusion of European allies, Russian representatives had previously suggested there was no space for European delegates at the table.

The announcement from Paris follows comments from United States President Donald Trump regarding a potential comprehensive deal with Russia concerning the wider European region. Mr Barrot emphasized that France intends to ensure that the perspective of Europe remains central during the diplomatic process. Previous diplomatic contacts have alternated between including and excluding European partners, but officials have insisted that this round will feature direct participation.

sections.heading: Diplomatic background and security concerns
paragraphs: The diplomatic maneuvering builds upon preparatory discussions held in Brussels on Thursday involving representatives from the United States, European nations, Ukraine, and the North Atlantic Treaty Organization. A spokesperson for the military alliance stated that those earlier meetings focused entirely on advancing a just and sustainable resolution to the war. United States presidential envoy Jared Kushner participated in the Brussels discussions via a video link, outlining broader American diplomatic objectives.

Mr Kushner indicated that Washington was actively pursuing a revised European security architecture designed to establish lasting peace conditions. However, this American approach has triggered anxiety among European allies who remain deeply suspicious of Moscow's long-term geopolitical ambitions. Before initiating the military invasion of Ukraine in 2022, the Kremlin issued sweeping demands that included the complete withdrawal of alliance troops from eastern Europe, which Western allies firmly rejected.

sections.heading: Differing stances among participating powers
paragraphs: The involvement of European nations highlights ongoing tensions over who dictates the terms of continental security arrangements. Moscow has historically sought to reshape the regional security framework to limit Western influence, a move firmly opposed by European capitals. Ukrainian leadership, conversely, has maintained that any lasting settlement must fully incorporate regional allies who bear the immediate fallout of the ongoing hostilities.

Washington has sought to balance direct negotiations with Moscow alongside consultations with its traditional allies across the Atlantic. Mr Kushner noted during the Brussels gathering that American officials would maintain close consultations with European partners on the sidelines of the Abu Dhabi discussions. Should meaningful progress materialize during the trilateral meetings, Washington aims to transition toward a broader multilateral format incorporating direct European participation.

sections.heading: Significance of the Abu Dhabi talks
paragraphs: The inclusion of European diplomats marks a critical turning point in the international management of the conflict and its ultimate resolution. Observers note that any lasting peace agreement must navigate complex security guarantees that directly impact the stability of the entire continent. The talks in the United Arab Emirates serve as a barometer for whether Washington and its partners can forge a unified diplomatic strategy moving forward.

Moreover, the discussions test the resilience of Western unity in the face of shifting political dynamics within the United States. European governments remain determined to safeguard their own strategic interests and prevent agreements being reached without their direct consent. The outcome of the scheduled sessions could dramatically alter the diplomatic landscape surrounding the protracted conflict.

sections.heading: Next steps in the diplomatic process
paragraphs: Delegates are preparing to convene in Abu Dhabi for the two days of scheduled talks starting on Tuesday. Security and foreign policy officials from the participating nations will test whether common ground can be found to halt hostilities. The degree of European involvement during these sessions will determine the framework for any subsequent diplomatic phases.

Following the conclusion of the mid-week meetings, international monitors will assess whether the discussions have laid the groundwork for an expanded multilateral summit. Western capitals will closely evaluate the substance of the Abu Dhabi talks to gauge the sincerity of the diplomatic overtures. Further announcements regarding the structure of future negotiations are expected once the current round concludes.
